issues.t: Timing belt snaps and bends valves
issues.sym: The engine suddenly dies while driving and will crank but not start. Some owners heard a knock or scraping noise first. Most failures happen between about 40,000 and 85,000 miles.
issues.why: The 1.6L engine uses a rubber timing belt, and when it breaks the pistons hit the valves (an "interference" engine). A failing tensioner or idler pulley can also throw the belt off. Repairs often mean bent valves and head work.
issues.next: If you do not have proof the belt was changed, replace the timing belt, tensioner, idler pulley and water pump now; do not wait past 60,000 miles. If it already broke, do not keep cranking the engine and get a quote for head repair versus a used engine.

issues.t: Timing belt idler pulley breaks
issues.sym: A squeal, rattle or grinding noise from the passenger side of the engine, followed by the engine stopping if the pulley breaks.
issues.why: The plastic or bearing-worn idler pulley on the timing belt can crack in half. When it does, the belt comes off and the valves can be damaged.
issues.next: Any noise from the timing belt area needs attention right away. Always replace the idler pulley and tensioner along with the belt.

issues.t: Burnt valves or cracked cylinder head
issues.sym: The engine runs rough, shakes, loses power and the check engine light flashes. A compression test shows one or more weak cylinders.
issues.why: Valves and the cylinder head on the 1.6L fail even without a broken timing belt. Owners report burnt valves and cracked heads around 60,000 to 70,000 miles.
issues.next: Do not drive far with a flashing check engine light. Ask a shop for a compression or leak-down test to confirm before paying for head work.

issues.t: Engine stalls or dies while driving
issues.sym: The engine shuts off while driving or idling with no clear pattern, then may restart after a few minutes.
issues.why: Shops have traced it to a failing crankshaft position sensor, the transmission or engine control module, and fuel pump problems. Many owners report several shop visits before it is found.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Note when it happens and have codes read right after a stall so the cause is easier to catch.

issues.t: Loses power, bucks or stalls
issues.sym: The car loses power, bucks or jerks, idles high, or stalls and then restarts. Sometimes the check engine light comes on.
issues.why: A dirty or failing throttle body and its sensor wiring are common causes. GM issued bulletins for a throttle body that sticks in cold, humid weather and for high idle fixed with a new sensor connector.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Have the codes read. Cleaning or replacing the throttle body, or repairing its connector, fixes many cars.

issues.t: Misfire from failed ignition coil
issues.sym: Rough running, hesitation, loss of power and a flashing check engine light.
issues.why: The one-piece ignition coil pack that fires all four spark plugs fails, often between 25,000 and 100,000 miles.
issues.next: Have the codes read. Replacing the coil pack, and the spark plugs if they are worn, usually fixes it.

issues.t: Oil leak into spark plug wells
issues.sym: Oil smell, oil on the top of the engine, and misfires or a check engine light once oil reaches the spark plugs.
issues.why: The valve cover gasket and spark plug tube seals harden with age and let oil into the spark plug wells.
issues.next: Replace the valve cover gasket and seals, and clean the plug wells. It is a simple fix that prevents misfires.

issues.t: Thermostat housing cracks and leaks coolant
issues.sym: Coolant drips or puddles, the coolant level drops, and the engine may overheat.
issues.why: The plastic thermostat housing cracks with heat and age. If the engine overheats, the cylinder head can be damaged.
issues.next: Watch the temperature gauge and pull over if it climbs. Replace the housing and thermostat as soon as a leak is found.

issues.t: Blown head gasket
issues.sym: White smoke from the exhaust, coolant loss with no visible leak, overheating, or a milky look to the oil.
issues.why: The head gasket fails, often after the engine has overheated. Some owners also found a cracked cylinder head.
issues.next: Stop driving if the engine overheats. A shop can do a cooling system pressure test and check for combustion gas in the coolant.

issues.t: A/C compressor fails
issues.sym: The A/C blows only warm air, sometimes suddenly on a hot day.
issues.why: The A/C compressor fails, and the condenser and drier are often replaced along with it.
issues.next: Have a shop check the system pressures to confirm the compressor is the problem before buying parts.

issues.t: Front-end rattle or pop over bumps
issues.sym: Rattles, creaks or a pop from the front end when going over bumps at low speed.
issues.why: Worn front control arm bushings and sway bar links. GM issued a bulletin about a front pop or rattle traced to the control arm.
issues.next: Have the front suspension inspected. Replacing worn links and bushings keeps the car aligned properly.

issues.t: Daytime running light module can overheat (recall)
issues.sym: A burning plastic smell or smoke from under the dash on the driver side, or daytime running lights that stop working.
issues.why: The daytime running light module can overheat and melt, which can start a fire (NHTSA 14V261000).
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and get the free repair right away. If you smell burning plastic, stop and turn the car off.

issues.t: Rear seat belt can lock up (recall)
issues.sym: A rear seat belt locks and will not pull out, so a passenger cannot buckle up.
issues.why: The rear seat belt retractor can lock in place (NHTSA 04V407000).
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and have the free repair done.

issues.t: Fuel line and fuse block crash fire risk (recall)
issues.sym: No warning signs.
issues.why: On some 2007 cars the fuel line and fuse block could be damaged in a crash in a way that raises fire risk (NHTSA 06V398000).
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: if you smell burning or see smoke, pull over where it's safe, turn the engine off, get everyone out and well away from the car, and leave the hood closed. Call 911 from a safe spot, even if you can't see flames. Don't drive it again until it has been repaired. Check your VIN for open recalls and have the free dealer repair done.

issues.t: Brake fluid can corrode ABS valve (recall)
issues.sym: The brake pedal travels farther than normal or the car takes longer to stop.
issues.why: Brake fluid can corrode a valve in the ABS unit on a small number of cars (NHTSA 14V460000).
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. Do not ignore a soft or long brake pedal.

issues.t: Key stuck or shifter will not leave Park
issues.sym: The key will not come out of the ignition, or the shifter will not move out of Park.
issues.why: The shift interlock that links the shifter and the key fails, often from a broken part in the shifter or a bad brake light switch.
issues.next: Check that the brake lights work, since the interlock needs that signal. A shop can repair or replace the shifter interlock.
issues.sevReason: Shifter stuck IN Park (interlock), not a rollaway; car cannot be driven, so no on-road hazard.

issues.t: Turn signals stop working
issues.sym: The turn signals do not work in one or both directions, or the indicator on the dash does not flash.
issues.why: The turn signal switch on the steering column wears out.
issues.next: Check the bulbs and flasher first. If they are fine, replace the turn signal switch.

issues.t: Airbag light stays on
issues.sym: The airbag warning light stays on or the passenger airbag status light acts up.
issues.why: A poor connection at the side airbag wiring under the seats is common, and GM issued a bulletin with an updated connector. The passenger seat sensor can also fail.
issues.next: The airbags may not work while the light is on. Have the codes read and the connector repaired.

issues.t: Check engine light for catalytic converter
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on with code P0420, sometimes with oxygen sensor lean codes.
issues.why: GM issued a bulletin for converter efficiency and oxygen sensor codes on this 1.6L. A worn converter or oxygen sensor is usually the cause.
issues.next: Have the codes read and the oxygen sensors tested first, before replacing the converter.

issues.t: Wind noise from doors
issues.sym: Whistling or chattering wind noise at highway speeds.
issues.why: Door seals and window glass that do not seal well against the body.
issues.next: A dealer or body shop can adjust the doors or windows and replace weak seals.

issues.t: Broken engine mount
issues.sym: Vibration in the cabin, a clunk when shifting or accelerating.
issues.why: An engine mount rubber tears and lets the engine move too much.
issues.next: Have the mounts inspected and replace the broken one.
